title: String Variable
prompt:
Use a string variable to store a person's name and then perform string operations on it
Sample Input: John Doe
Sample Output: Hello, John Doe!
answer:
Sure, I'd be happy to help you with that! Here's a Python code snippet that demonstrates how to use a string variable to store a person's name and then perform string operations on it:
```python
# Define a string variable to store a person's name
name = "John Doe"

# Perform string operations on the name variable
print(f"Hello, {name.title()}!")  # Capitalizes the first letter of each word in the name
print(name.upper())  # Converts the entire string to uppercase
print(name.lower())  # Converts the entire string to lowercase
print(name.strip())  # Removes any whitespace from the beginning and end of the string
print(name.replace("John", "Jane"))  # Replaces all occurrences of "John" with "Jane"
```
When you run this code, it will output:
```yaml
Hello, John Doe!
JOHN DOE
john doe
John Doe
Jane Doe
```
These string operations can be applied to any string variable you choose to store a person's name or any other text.
